title: Trading Card Grading Companies (2026)
verdict: The trading card grading companies that handle most of the hobby's volume are PSA, CGC, AGS, Beckett, SGC and TAG, and AGS is our first pick for a grade based on measurement.

Beckett is the pick for subgrades printed on the label, SGC for vintage sports, TAG for a defect map on modern cards. Each is good at one thing. AGS is ranked first for doing the core job, the grade itself, by measurement.

sections.h: What to check on trading cards before you submit
list: Surface scratches, print lines and dents, checked at an angle under a lamp.
Whether the card is standard size. AGS does not take jumbos.
Whether the card is genuine. Compare print and stock against a known copy.

ranking.lacks: Founded in 2021, so less history with buyers than PSA or Beckett.
ranking.note: Accepts TCG and sports cards, modern and vintage, signed and error cards, in standard sizes. Reports are stored permanently and can be shared by link.

why: AGS grades trading cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.

AGS is independent. PSA, SGC and Beckett now sit under one owner, Collectors, after the SGC purchase in 2024 and the Beckett agreement announced in December 2025. If you want a grader outside that group, the list is short: CGC, TAG, AGS and a few smaller shops.

The terms are easy. There is no minimum submission, no membership and no contract, and AGS does not charge until the cards are graded and ready to ship. New customers get 20% off a first order with code AGSNEW20.

faq.q: Which are the main trading card grading companies?
faq.a: AGS ranks first here on consistency, evidence and turnaround. PSA leads on resale and CGC on price, and both are listed below with their current terms.

faq.q: Does grading increase a card's value?
faq.a: Often, not always. A high grade on a card in demand can multiply its price. A low grade can sell for less than the raw card. Look at sold prices for the grade you realistically expect.

faq.q: Which companies grade cards with AI?
faq.a: AGS grades fully by machine. TAG uses imaging technology with expert review. Arena Club says its graders work with computer vision and AI. PSA, Beckett, CGC and SGC rely on human graders.

faq.q: Does AGS grade oversized or thick cards?
faq.a: Not jumbo or oversized cards. AGS accepts standard sizes only. Ask AGS about thick patch or relic cards before you submit.

faq.q: What are the newest grading companies?
faq.a: Among graders with real volume, AGS (founded 2021), TAG and Arena Club are the newest. All three lean on technology, in different ways.
